summary.en: An ambush in eastern DR Congo has killed or injured about 20 people, including former UFC fighter Tim Kennedy and a retired US Green Beret, while a former New Zealand special forces officer was also killed. The attack involved forces linked to Erik Prince’s security firm, highlighting the growing presence of private mercenary groups in the region. This incident follows a pattern of intensified fighting tied to the M23 rebel campaign, which has escalated since its 2022 resurgence. The latest violence underscores a widening conflict beyond traditional state actors, adding a new dimension of foreign‑run security forces to the crisis. According to UCDP, there were 1,158 battle‑related deaths in 2024.
summary.nb: Et bakholdsangrep i Øst‑DR Kongo har drept eller såret omtrent 20 personer, blant dem den tidligere UFC‑utøveren Tim Kennedy og en pensjonert amerikansk Green Beret, mens en tidligere nyzealandsk spesialstyrkeoffiser også ble drept. Angrepet ble utført av styrker knyttet til Erik Princes sikkerhetsfirma, noe som fremhever den økende tilstedeværelsen av private leiesoldatgrupper i regionen. Hendelsen følger et mønster av intensivering av kampene knyttet til M23‑opprørsbevegelsen, som har eskalert siden oppblomstringen i 2022. Den siste volden understreker en utvidelse av konflikten utover tradisjonelle statlige aktører, og tilfører en ny dimensjon av utenlandsstyrte sikkerhetsstyrker til krisen. Ifølge UCDP var det 1 158 dødsfall i kamprelaterte handlinger i 2024.

background.title: M23 campaign (2022–present)
background.extract: The M23 campaign is an ongoing series of military offensives launched by the March 23 Movement (M23), a Rwandan-backed rebel paramilitary group in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, since March 2022. In November 2021, M23 first launched attacks against the Congolese military (FARDC) and MONUSCO, seizing military positions in Ndiza, Cyanzu, and Runyoni in North Kivu Province. This coincided with the deployment of Uganda People's Defence Force (UPDF) to the region to combat the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), a Ugandan rebel group operating in the Congo's North Kivu and Ituri provinces.
